newsitem.title: FRANCE: L'Oreal study if Synthelabo needs partner.
newsitem.headline: L'Oreal study if Synthelabo needs partner.

text.p: Cosmetics group L'Oreal is constantly studying whether its Synthelabo drugs subsidiary can develop on its own in the long run or needs an alliance, L'Oreal chairman Lindsay Owen-Jones said in an interview on Monday.

"There is the issue of Synthelabo's long term outlook, and notably whether it can develop on its own or if it needs to associate itself" with another group, he told the newspaper Le Figaro. "I feel that up to now it has proven perfectly capable of developing. But it's clear this is a permanent discussion."
He said there was no reason for L'Oreal to shed Synthelabo now, noting that the drugs unit's value had risen in 1996.

"That said, we've never set for ourselves the objective of becoming a global leader in pharmaceuticals, and it would be out of the question to upset the balance of our group by investing massively in pharmaceuticals to the detriment of our core business, cosmetics," he said.
"We've always felt that owning a pharmaceuticals subsidiary was a way to better manage our core business. Without any doubt, Synthelabo has helped us develop," Owen-Jones said.
